newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Shenzhen B shares close up on improved sentiment.
newsitem.headline: Shenzhen B shares close up on improved sentiment.

text.p: Shenzhen's B share index ended up on Friday, supported by official reports that Shenzhen securities authorities and officials from major listed firms are stepping up efforts to promote B shares, brokers said.
The B share index gained 1.4 points or 0.92 percent to 153.15 points on turnover of HK$87 million, down from Thursday's 93 million.

The Shenzhen-based Securities Times said on Friday a delegation headed by Liu Xinhua, director of Shenzhen Securities Management Office, left on Thursday to promote B share issues to overseas investors.
"Market sentiment was improved by the news, which reflects the government's attitude towards the B share market," a broker said.
"This is certainly good news for the B share market," an analyst with a major Chinese brokerage said. "If successful, it will lead to an expanded base of B share investors."
But, he said, some investors stayed on the sidelines ahead of the weekend, leading to lower turnover for the day.
Brokers said they expected the market to move slowly higher early next week, with buying focussing on companies expected to post good 1996 results.
China Bicycle was the best performer on institutional buying, rising HK$0.15 or 4.41 percent to HK$3.55 on heaviest trade of 2.03 million shares on institutional buying, brokers said.
Textile concern Shenzhen Victor Onward gained HK$0.10 to HK$3.08 with 189,703 shares changing hands.
The A share index firmed 3.06 points or 0.81 percent to close at 382.63 points on turnover of 9.54 billion yuan, compared with Thursday's 9.67 billion yuan.
Brokers said they expected the gains to extend into next week.
